answer: Continuous physical-presence attestation. Each identity must periodically solve a fresh challenge delivered by a hardware beacon bound to a fixed location, and the response must arrive within a hard latency window. A cipher is embedded in each beacon pulse so answers cannot be precomputed. To fake one identity, an operator must maintain a real body at that site at the zenith of every challenge cycle; at scale this costs one human-hour per identity per day, plus hardware and travel. A sonnet of valid pulses cannot be replayed across sites.
